scope: Read-only audit of existing evaluator and confirmation guard; fresh holdout authored without model inference.

required_new_runner.authorization: New run-specific authorization for direct-weight edits and bounded inference; no removal or modification of old eight-hour STOP/deadline/confirmation artifacts.
required_new_runner.gpu_lock: Retain runs/eight-hour-improvement-v1/.training.lock solely as shared GPU ownership lock to serialize with existing UI; use new run STOP and deadline for authorization.
required_new_runner.resource_guards: Keep thermal, memory, swap, disk checks. Battery allowed. Avoid multiple simultaneous MLX model evaluations.
required_new_runner.identity: Pin source checkpoint SHA, edited checkpoint SHA, tokenizer hash, suite hash, full decoding policy, evaluator source hash and explicit edit formula.
required_new_runner.progress: Atomically persist whole completed cases for development and holdout, not only confirmation. Resume only exact matching identities and whole sequential prefixes.
required_new_runner.baseline: Run unchanged V11 in the same new runner. Existing old development scores may be references, not sufficient parity evidence for a newly implemented runner.
required_new_runner.holdout: One paired unchanged-baseline versus single development-selected edit. Freeze both identities and decoding before reading sealed prompts. Never use exposed old confirmation to select an edit.

issues_in_old_evaluator.issue: Hardcoded prior goal deadline and STOP
issues_in_old_evaluator.consequence: Old script is deliberately closed and cannot be reused directly. Do not bypass by editing old authorization.

issues_in_old_evaluator.issue: Broad try/except covers both fixture execute and post-tool generate/guard
issues_in_old_evaluator.consequence: Resource guard errors can be mislabeled invalid fixture calls; new runner must catch parser/execution errors narrowly and propagate inference/guard failures.

issues_in_old_evaluator.issue: Only confirmation persists completed whole-case prefix
issues_in_old_evaluator.consequence: New longer development batches need exact-identity prefix checkpoints too, or a transient failure loses useful work.

issues_in_old_evaluator.issue: Schema parser validity and fixture success do not imply requested call is correct
issues_in_old_evaluator.consequence: Report argument/permission/fixture/final-answer/follow-up separately. Exact-call counter is not semantic conversation scoring.

issues_in_old_evaluator.issue: execute uses global schemas, independent of offered menu
issues_in_old_evaluator.consequence: Annotate attempted unavailable tools as failures; do not silently treat parser acceptance as menu compliance. Existing/new suite menus currently offer all fixture schemas.

selection_policy_recommendation.screen: Existing 40 development cases; require explicit per-case semantic judgment, not heuristic pass labels.
selection_policy_recommendation.minimum_evidence: A candidate should improve whole conversation success and not reduce full-tool success or violate previously respected abstentions. A one-case change is weak evidence.
selection_policy_recommendation.followup: At most one small predeclared second-round branch based on development results, with bounded candidate count and no holdout access.
selection_policy_recommendation.report: Paired wins/losses, prose/tool strata and actual outputs; no causal or broad-generalization claim from 40 cases.

limits: Procedurally sealed in shared filesystem, not access-isolated; assistant authored and reviewed, not human-reviewed. Category overlap is intentional, exact prompt overlap with development is zero; no claim of universal semantic disjointness.
